name: Simulation
subtitle: Generate observable world behavior via system rules; the core is variables, causal chains, and explainability.
demoRuleHint: Example rule: Set resource generation rate → Observe population growth → Adjust resource allocation.
problemsSolved: Make causal chains observable and explainable, avoiding 'black-box number crunching'.
Provide steady states and boundary conditions to prevent system runaway or boring stagnation.
Give players clear intervention levers (parameters/strategies/resources) so adjustments are effective.
learningGoals: Understand how core variables and causal chains drive outcomes.
Master explainability: let players know why things happen.
Be able to design controllable emergent behavior, avoiding runaway and boredom.
minimalRules: Observation: Let players see key metric changes.
systemLoopHint: Input (parameters/strategies) → Evolution (rule updates) → Observation (metric changes) → Decision (success/failure) → Adjustment → New input

combos.effect: Drive system evolution and expansion with long-term goals.
Alter system trajectory through key decisions.
More realistic world rules bring emergent gameplay.

advancedWarnings: Too many variables reduce explainability; too few variables reduce depth.
Long feedback cycles cause players to lose immediate feedback; short cycles cause excessive system noise.
Overly restricting parameters can spur players to find micro-tuning points, producing richer emergent behavior—limits force exploration of edge states.
advancedAlgoRefs: Evolution: tick updates, event queue, stability control.

demoLab.title: Tax Lever Experiment
demoLab.action: Drag the "Tax Rate" slider from 0.2 to 0.5, "Advance (tick)" 10 days, and watch money and happiness diverge
demoLab.observe: The tax rate is the start of the causal chain: money surges while happiness slides, and low happiness in turn suppresses pop growth. One lever moves several metrics — the depth of simulation play comes from the propagation delay between variables

demoLab.title: Steady-State Hunt
demoLab.action: Use "Raise Tax (primary)" / "Cut Tax (secondary)" to fine-tune, hunting for the tax band where happiness and money both rise
demoLab.observe: The system reaches a steady state at middle tax rates — both extremes collapse (0% starves the treasury, 60% drives people away). An observable steady-state boundary makes "adjustment works": players find their own optimum instead of memorizing a guide

demoLab.title: Collapse Watch
demoLab.action: Push the tax rate to 0.6 and "Advance (tick)" for 20 straight days
demoLab.observe: happiness collapses → pop drains → tax revenue actually falls — a Laffer-curve counterintuitive: maximum rate ≠ maximum revenue. Emergent collapse is the core teaching moment of simulation play: when causal chains are observable, collapse becomes explainable
